notesEn.CYP: The OECD database does not cover Cyprus, so the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) real residential property price index is used instead (deflated by consumer prices; national source: Central Bank of Cyprus)

notesEn.CAN: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) real residential property price index (a different national series, deflated by consumer prices) shows +24% over the 10 years to 2025, against +40% from the OECD: the two use different source series or deflators
notesEn.CHE: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) real residential property price index (a different national series, deflated by consumer prices) shows +26% over the 10 years to 2025, against +36% from the OECD: the two use different source series or deflators
notesEn.CHN: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) real residential property price index (a different national series, deflated by consumer prices) shows -5% over the 10 years to 2025, against +37% from the OECD: the two use different source series or deflators
notesEn.HUN: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) real residential property price index (a different national series, deflated by consumer prices) shows +115% over the 10 years to 2025, against +102% from the OECD: the two use different source series or deflators
notesEn.KOR: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) real residential property price index (a different national series, deflated by consumer prices) shows +3% over the 10 years to 2025, against -9% from the OECD: the two use different source series or deflators
notesEn.RUS: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) real residential property price index (a different national series, deflated by consumer prices) shows +19% over the 10 years to 2025, against +111% from the OECD: the two use different source series or deflators
notesEn.TUR: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) real residential property price index (a different national series, deflated by consumer prices) shows +86% over the 10 years to 2025, against +68% from the OECD: the two use different source series or deflators
notesEn.USA: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) real residential property price index (a different national series, deflated by consumer prices) shows +38% over the 10 years to 2025, against +54% from the OECD: the two use different source series or deflators
notesEn.TWN: Taiwan is not covered by the OECD or the BIS; the Ministry of the Interior's housing price index (based on actual transaction prices, from the third quarter of 2012) is divided by DGBAS's consumer price index. The index only starts in 2012, so 10-year changes begin in 2023
